key_insight: Mem++ changes LLM agent memory from “compress at write time” to “select at read time,” preserving full document history so answers can reflect the correct version at a given time.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for organizational AI systems that need auditable, time-aware memory across evolving documents, decisions, and revisions without losing older context.
method: Stores every document in full with date and author metadata.
Performs retrieval only over documents available up to the question’s time.
Fuses lexical and semantic ranking signals at read time instead of generating summaries during ingestion.
evidence_signal: On OrgMemBench, Mem++ outperformed the strongest memory baseline by 8.0–13.1 points across two answering models, and with gpt-4.1-mini it beat RAG by 2.6 points overall.
watch_item: Keeping all documents intact may increase storage and retrieval complexity, so performance depends on careful indexing and time-filtering implementation.
paper_title: Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents
